A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Generative Montage and CoPHEME study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite added sections and pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original CoPHEME simulations, downstream deception results, component ablations, sequence-length experiments and production-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including evaluations of 14 LLMs and the accompanying ablations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The Writer–Editor–Director framework, adversarial debate loops, Sybil dissemination and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. Appendix A.5 documents victim behavior without establishing a change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six CoPHEME rumor events and text-based belief manipulation and downstream verification tasks. Additional domains and multimodal settings are discussed only as future work.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the full model, w/o Debate, w/o Editor and Single-Agent configurations. The downstream comparisons still use Majority Vote and AI Judge; newly cited defenses are not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: The evaluated models, five-victim protocol, metrics, 0.8 high-confidence threshold and 1–20-post sequence-length sweep remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 newly explains prompting and scoring rather than revising a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: The component ablations, sequence-length analysis, efficiency analysis and six pipeline examples are retained. The added A.5 walkthrough explains scoring using an existing Charlie Hebdo example; it supplies no additional empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent victims per target and report mean ± standard deviation across attack instances in Table 5. No seed information, repeated-run counts or statistical reporting practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the result figures retain their numerical values and findings, including the reported 74.4% proprietary-model and 70.6% open-weights-model average ASRs. The new scoring illustration does not report an additional experiment.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, optimization objectives, Equations 1–16 and appendix complexity expression are retained. The defense discussion and scoring walkthrough introduce no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims concerning cognitive collusion, Generative Montage, CoPHEME, reasoning-related susceptibility and downstream misinformation cascades. The proposed defenses are not presented as validated contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 6 expands v1's brief defense suggestions with hypotheses involving belief trajectories, entropy, cross-model divergence and provenance auditing. Future-work scope is also refined, while interpretations of existing results and the central limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.5 specifies structured victim outputs, initial claim formation before questioning about the target hypothesis, and direct verdict-based ASR scoring. Appendix A also explicitly identifies example prompts as available in the existing codebase.

R1.justification: The cited literature substantially expands into defensive monitoring, entropy, provenance and unlearning, especially in Section 6, alongside additional work on truthful deception and multi-agent persuasion. Examples include Beigi, Farquhar, Feng, Kang and Dogra; the core novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 adds the defense section, victim-configuration subsection and acknowledgments, revises the limitations, and updates author contact information and section numbering. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The same four figures, six tables and two algorithm boxes are retained. There are layout and placement changes, including reflowed algorithm boxes and a resized Table 6 placed on a separate final page.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.5 improves transparency about when victims encounter the target hypothesis and how attack success is scored, addressing an ambiguity in v1. The defense discussion adds useful research context. These are limited gains: the defenses remain untested, and the empirical evidence and core scientific conclusions are unchanged.
